newsitem.title: UK: London gold recovers from fresh low by PM fixing.
newsitem.headline: London gold recovers from fresh low by PM fixing.

text.p: Gold prices plunged to a 3-3/4 year low on Wednesday before recovering slightly after a nervous wait for New York, dealer said.
"When it got down to $336.50 the market was extremely nervous and most people squared off for New York's opening," one dealer said.
New York's Comex gapped lower early, steadied but fresh weakness came in as as bullion came up to around $338.00 per ounce.
Gold fixed at $337.70 per ounce Wednesday afternoon compared with $336.90 this morning and $339.40 on Tuesday.
Around the fixing, New York's April contract was showing a deficit of $2.00 on the close at $339.90.
Dealers said the slightly easier U.S. dollar took some of the pressure off the ailing gold market.
A surge in the U.S. currency's value on Tuesday was part of the reason for unwinding of gold and silver positions which took most of the precious metals to negative closes.
One dealer said there has been a few bids at the lower levels but selling was unrelented. "There are just very few buyers around," he said.
Another said gold seemed to have found a bit of support around $336 earlier which might have had more to do with a nervous market squaring its positions than any technical issue.
"The charts suggest a major correction is due but if the funds decide $336 is no good, then we could see $330 very quickly," he said.
That would put gold within sight of its seven-year low of $326.10 fix reached on March 10, 1993 before its brief bull run to $406.70 on August 2 that year.
The other metals were mixed with silver also off its low at $4.86/$4.88 but still down six cents.
Palladium fixed at a fresh 10-month high of $136.65 as it continued to get support from the hedge funds on top of consumer buying against the delayed Russia-Japan 1997 supply contract talks.
The Russian upper house passing the country's budget today could inch the beginning of negotiations slightly closer, dealers said.
"Palladium is a fund-led market now. They took their profits yesterday and bought back in all within minutes," a dealer said.
Platinum was at $357.30/$358.30 up $2.80 and taking advantage of a widening premium over gold.
